records.source: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם כִּסְאִ֔י וְהָאָ֖רֶץ הֲדֹ֣ם רַגְלָ֑י אֵי־זֶ֥ה בַ֨יִת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּבְנוּ־לִ֔י וְאֵי־זֶ֥ה מָק֖וֹם מְנוּחָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: The heavens [are] my throne, and the earth [is the] footstool of my feet. Where [is] this house that you will build for me, and where [is] this place of my rest?
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: The heavens are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne, \q and the earth is a stool for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet. \q What kind of house would you build for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and what kind of place could be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} resting place?

L.1: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: The heavens [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne, \q and the earth [is] the footstool of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet. \q Where [is] this house that you would build for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and where [is] this place of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rest?

R.1: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Heaven is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne, \q and the earth is where I rest {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet. \q So what kind of house could you build for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q What kind of place could you make for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to rest in?

decisions.choice: heaven as God's throne and the earth as his footstool: no building can contain him
decisions.reason: Solomon said at the dedication of the temple that heaven itself cannot contain God, much less a house (1 Kings 8:27). Stephen quotes this verse and the next in Acts 7:49-50, and Jesus speaks of heaven as God's throne and the earth as his footstool in Matthew 5:34-35.

decisions.choice: where is this house: what sort of house could be fit for me
decisions.reason: The question can ask where the house is or what kind of house it would be. Either way it expects no answer: nothing people build can be a fitting home for the Maker of heaven and earth (2 Samuel 7:5-7).

decisions.choice: the place of my rest: the temple, God's dwelling among his people
decisions.reason: The temple is called God's resting place in Psalm 132:8, 14 and 1 Chronicles 28:2, where the ark is the footstool of God's feet. The verse does not reject the temple (verse 6; 56:7) but rejects the idea that God needs it.

decisions.choice: where I rest my feet
decisions.reason: Readable explains "footstool" by saying what a footstool is for.

records.heading: Heaven is God's throne

records.source: וְאֶת־כָּל־אֵ֨לֶּה֙ יָדִ֣י עָשָׂ֔תָה וַיִּהְי֥וּ כָל־אֵ֖לֶּה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶל־זֶ֣ה אַבִּ֔יט אֶל־עָנִי֙ וּנְכֵה־ר֔וּחַ וְחָרֵ֖ד עַל־דְּבָרִֽי׃
records.gloss: And all these [things] my hand made, and all these [things] came to be, declares Yahweh; and to this [one] I will look: to [the] afflicted and stricken of spirit, and trembling at my word.
pieces: My own hand made all these things, \q and that is how they all exist, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q The one I will regard with favor is the lowly, the broken in spirit, \q who trembles at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word.

L.2: And all these [things] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand made, \q and all these [things] came into being, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q But to this [one] I will look: \q to [the] afflicted and stricken in spirit, \q and trembling at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word.

R.2: I made all these things myself, \q and that is why they exist, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I am pleased with people who are humble and whose spirit is broken, \q people who tremble with awe at what I say.

decisions.choice: and all these came to be: everything exists because God made it
decisions.reason: The clause gives the result of God's making: the heavens and the earth of verse 1 exist only because his hand made them (Genesis 1). The Septuagint reads "and all these are mine".

decisions.choice: I will look to: I will regard with favor; afflicted and stricken in spirit: lowly and humbled before God
decisions.reason: To look to someone is to pay attention to him with favor (Genesis 4:4-5). The one God looks to is not the builder of a grand house but the poor and humbled person (57:15; Psalm 34:19; 51:19).

decisions.choice: trembling at my word: taking God's word with deep reverence and fear of disobeying it
decisions.reason: The same people are addressed in verse 5 and in Ezra 9:4 and 10:3, where those who tremble at God's commands are those who obey them.

decisions.choice: I am pleased with
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "I will look to" means here: God looks with favor.

records.source: שׁוֹחֵ֨ט הַשּׁ֜וֹר מַכֵּה־אִ֗ישׁ זוֹבֵ֤חַ הַשֶּׂה֙ עֹ֣רֵֽף כֶּ֔לֶב מַעֲלֵ֤ה מִנְחָה֙ דַּם־חֲזִ֔יר מַזְכִּ֥יר לְבֹנָ֖ה מְבָ֣רֵֽךְ אָ֑וֶן גַּם־הֵ֗מָּה בָּֽחֲרוּ֙ בְּדַרְכֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְשִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֖ם נַפְשָׁ֥ם חָפֵֽצָה׃
records.gloss: [One] slaughtering the ox, striking a man; sacrificing the lamb, breaking a dog's neck; offering up a grain offering, pig's blood; making a memorial of frankincense, blessing wickedness. Also they have chosen their ways, and in their detestable things their soul delights.
pieces: Slaughtering an ox is no different from killing a person; \q sacrificing a lamb, from breaking a dog's neck; \q presenting a grain offering, from offering pig's blood; \q burning frankincense as a memorial, from blessing an idol. \q These people have chosen their own ways, \q and their hearts delight in their loathsome things.

L.3: [One who] slaughters the ox [is like one who] strikes down a man; \q [one who] sacrifices the lamb, [like one who] breaks a dog's neck; \q [one who] offers up a grain offering, [like one who offers] pig's blood; \q [one who] burns frankincense as a memorial, [like one who] blesses an idol. \q They also have chosen their [own] ways, \q and their soul delights in their detestable things.

R.3: When these people kill an ox as a sacrifice, it is as bad as murdering someone. When they sacrifice a lamb, it is as bad as breaking a dog's neck. \q When they bring a grain offering, it is like offering the blood of a pig. \q When they burn sweet incense as an offering, it is like worshiping an idol. \q They have chosen to go their own way, \q and they love the disgusting things they do.

decisions.choice: one who slaughters an ox is like one who kills a person: each lawful sacrifice is set beside a crime and counted as no better
alternatives: the same people who sacrifice an ox also kill a person
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets each pair side by side with no verb. Read as a comparison, the verse says that when people who do not tremble at God's word (verse 2) bring sacrifices, God counts them as murder and idolatry (1:11-15). It can also be read as two acts of the same people: they sacrifice an ox and also kill a person, offer a lamb and also a dog. The comparison is taken here; the sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: dog and pig: unclean animals that could never be offered
decisions.reason: The pig was unclean (Leviticus 11:7; Deuteronomy 14:8), and a dog's price could not be brought into God's house (Deuteronomy 23:19). Breaking the neck was how the firstborn of a donkey was killed when it was not redeemed (Exodus 13:13). See also 65:4 and 66:17.

decisions.choice: burns frankincense as a memorial: the memorial portion of the grain offering; blesses an idol: honors a false god
decisions.reason: The verb is linked to the "memorial portion" burned with frankincense (Leviticus 2:2). The word for "wickedness" is used for idols and idolatry (1 Samuel 15:23; Hosea 10:5, 8, where Beth-el is mocked as Beth-aven, "house of wickedness").

decisions.choice: is no different from
decisions.reason: Balanced expresses the comparison of meaning decision m1 with "is no different from" rather than repeating "is like" in every line.

decisions.choice: When these people ...; it is as bad as; burn sweet incense as an offering
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison explicit as "it is as bad as" and names who is meant. It explains frankincense as sweet incense.

records.source: גַּם־אֲנִ֞י אֶבְחַ֣ר בְּתַעֲלֻלֵיהֶ֗ם וּמְגֽוּרֹתָם֙ אָבִ֣יא לָהֶ֔ם יַ֤עַן קָרָ֨אתִי֙ וְאֵ֣ין עוֹנֶ֔ה דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי וְלֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ וַיַּעֲשׂ֤וּ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־חָפַ֖צְתִּי בָּחָֽרוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Also I will choose their harsh dealings, and their fears I will bring to them, because I called and there was none answering, I spoke and they did not listen; and they did the evil in my eyes, and in what I did not delight they chose.
pieces: So I in turn will choose how harshly to deal with them and will bring on them the very things they fear. \q For when I called, no one replied; \q when I spoke, they would not listen. \q They did what was evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight \q and chose what gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no pleasure.

L.4: I also will choose their harsh treatment, and what they dread I will bring on them, \q because I called and no one answered, \q I spoke and they did not listen; \q and they did what [was] evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes, \q and what I did not delight in they chose.

R.4: So I will choose how to punish them. I will make the things they are afraid of happen to them. \q I called to them, but no one answered. \q I spoke, but they did not listen. \q They did what I consider evil. \q They chose to do things that do not please {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: they have chosen ... I also will choose: God answers their choice with his own
decisions.reason: Verse 3 ends "they too have chosen", and verse 4 begins "I too will choose". The repeated verb shows that God's judgment matches what the people chose.

decisions.choice: harsh treatment: dealings that make sport of them, punishments that fit their folly
decisions.reason: The noun occurs elsewhere only in 3:4, where it refers to capricious or childish rulers. Here it means God's harsh dealing with those who made a mockery of worship. The exact sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: I called and no one answered: the same charge as 65:12
decisions.reason: The last four lines repeat 65:12 almost word for word, tying the two chapters together. See also 50:2.

decisions.choice: how to punish them; what I consider evil
decisions.reason: Readable says "punish" for the harsh treatment and explains "evil in my eyes".

records.source: שִׁמְעוּ֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה הַחֲרֵדִ֖ים אֶל־דְּבָר֑וֹ אָמְרוּ֩ אֲחֵיכֶ֨ם שֹׂנְאֵיכֶ֜ם מְנַדֵּיכֶ֗ם לְמַ֤עַן שְׁמִי֙ יִכְבַּ֣ד יְהוָ֔ה וְנִרְאֶ֥ה בְשִׂמְחַתְכֶ֖ם וְהֵ֥ם יֵבֹֽשׁוּ׃
records.gloss: Hear [the] word of Yahweh, the [ones] trembling at his word: Your brothers have said, [those] hating you, [those] thrusting you out for the sake of my name, Let Yahweh be glorified, and we will look on your joy; and they will be ashamed.
pieces: Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q you who tremble at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word: \q Your own kin, who hate you and cast you out because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, have said, "Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, \q and we will see how glad you are!" But it is they who will be put to shame.

L.5: Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q [you who] tremble at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word: \q {{gender:Your brothers and sisters|Your brothers}} who hate you, who thrust you out for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, have said, "Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be glorified, \q so that we may see your joy!" But they will be put to shame.

R.5: Listen to the message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q you who tremble with awe at what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says. \q Your own people hate you. They push you away because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They say, "Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} show how great {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is! \q Then we will see you happy!" But they are the ones who will be put to shame.

decisions.choice: your brothers: fellow Israelites who reject the faithful
decisions.reason: The faithful who tremble at God's word (verse 2) are hated and shut out by members of their own people. Jesus speaks of the same treatment in Luke 6:22.

decisions.choice: for the sake of my name: they exclude the faithful because of their loyalty to God
alternatives: claiming to act for the sake of my name
decisions.reason: The phrase may describe why the faithful are cast out (because they bear God's name) or the excuse of those who cast them out (they claim to act for God's name). Either way the faithful suffer for the LORD.

decisions.choice: Let the LORD be glorified, so that we may see your joy: a mocking taunt
decisions.reason: The words dare God to act and the faithful to show the joy they hope for. God's answer comes in verses 6-14, where the mockers are shamed and the faithful rejoice.

decisions.choice: because you belong to me
decisions.reason: Readable explains "for the sake of my name" as the reason the faithful are rejected: they are God's people.

records.heading: Zion's children born in a day

records.source: ק֤וֹל שָׁאוֹן֙ מֵעִ֔יר ק֖וֹל מֵֽהֵיכָ֑ל ק֣וֹל יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁלֵּ֥ם גְּמ֖וּל לְאֹיְבָֽיו׃
records.gloss: [The] sound of an uproar from [the] city, a sound from [the] temple, [the] sound of Yahweh repaying recompense to his enemies.
pieces: Hear that roar from the city! \q Hear the noise from the temple! \q It is the sound of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} paying back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies what they have earned.

L.6: A sound of uproar from the city! \q A sound from the temple! \q The sound of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} paying back recompense to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies!

R.6: Listen! There is a loud noise coming from the city and from the temple. \q It is the noise of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} punishes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies as they deserve.

decisions.choice: a sound: an exclamation calling for attention, "Listen!"
decisions.reason: The repeated word can mean "sound" or work as an exclamation, "Listen!" (40:3, 6; 52:8). Here it announces the noise of God's coming in judgment.

decisions.choice: the temple: God's house in Jerusalem, from which his judgment goes out
decisions.reason: The LORD acts from his temple (Amos 1:2; Micah 1:2). The word can also mean a palace, but beside "the city" it is the temple on Mount Zion.

records.source: בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּחִ֖יל יָלָ֑דָה בְּטֶ֨רֶם יָב֥וֹא חֵ֛בֶל לָ֖הּ וְהִמְלִ֥יטָה זָכָֽר׃
records.gloss: Before she was in labor she gave birth; before pain came to her, and she delivered a male.
pieces: Before her labor began, she gave birth; \q before the pangs came over her, she brought a son into the world.

L.7: Before she was in labor, she gave birth; \q before [the] pain came to her, she delivered a male [child].

R.7: Zion is like a woman who gives birth before her labor even starts. \q Before she feels any pain, she has a baby boy.

decisions.choice: she: Zion, the mother city, whose son is a restored people
decisions.reason: Verse 8 names the mother as Zion. The sudden painless birth pictures God giving Jerusalem a new people all at once (49:20-21; 54:1).

decisions.choice: gave birth, delivered: the coming event told as already done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form used for completed action; the prophet speaks of the future as certain, as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: Zion is like a woman who
decisions.reason: Readable names the mother, as verse 8 does, and makes the picture a comparison.

records.source: מִֽי־שָׁמַ֣ע כָּזֹ֗את מִ֤י רָאָה֙ כָּאֵ֔לֶּה הֲי֤וּחַל אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּי֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד אִם־יִוָּ֥לֵֽד גּ֖וֹי פַּ֣עַם אֶחָ֑ת כִּֽי־חָ֛לָה גַּם־יָלְדָ֥ה צִיּ֖וֹן אֶת־בָּנֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Who has heard like this? Who has seen like these? Will a land be brought to birth in one day? Or will a nation be born [at] one time? For she was in labor, also she gave birth, Zion, to her children.
pieces: Who ever heard of anything like this? Who has seen the like? \q Is a country brought to birth in a single day, \q or a nation born in one moment? \q Yet Zion had barely begun her labor when she bore her children.

L.8: Who has heard [anything] like this? Who has seen [things] like these? \q Will a land be brought to birth in one day? \q Or will a nation be born at one time? \q Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.

R.8: No one has ever heard of anything like this! No one has ever seen such things! \q A whole country cannot be born in a single day. \q A nation cannot come into being in a moment. \q But as soon as Zion's labor began, her children were born.

decisions.choice: as soon as she was in labor, she gave birth: labor and birth came together
decisions.reason: The words "for ... also" join the two verbs so that the birth follows the first pain at once. This answers the questions: what never happens in nature God will do for Zion.

decisions.choice: her children: the people of Zion, gathered and restored
decisions.reason: Zion's children are her inhabitants and the exiles who return to her (49:17-22; 54:1-3; 60:4).

decisions.choice: A whole country cannot be born ... A nation cannot come into being
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions, which expect the answer "no", into statements.

records.source: הַאֲנִ֥י אַשְׁבִּ֛יר וְלֹ֥א אוֹלִ֖יד יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אִם־אֲנִ֧י הַמּוֹלִ֛יד וְעָצַ֖רְתִּי אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃ס
records.gloss: Do I bring to the breaking-point and not cause to give birth? says Yahweh. Or [am] I the [one] causing to give birth and I shut? says your God.
pieces: Would I bring on the birth and then not let the child be born? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Would I, who bring children to birth, then hold them back? says your God.

L.9: Will I bring to the point of breaking and not cause to give birth? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Or [am] I the one who causes to give birth, and [then] I shut [the womb]? says your God.

R.9: I would never bring a mother to the moment of birth and then stop her baby from being born, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I am the one who makes birth happen. I would never close the womb, says your God.

decisions.choice: bring to the breaking point and not cause to give birth: God reverses the lament of 37:3
decisions.reason: In 37:3 Hezekiah said, "Children have come to the breaking point, and there is no strength to give birth." The same rare root for the opening of the womb returns here: what Judah could not do then, God will do for Zion.

decisions.choice: shut: close the womb, hold back the birth
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God closing the womb (Genesis 16:2; 20:18). Both questions expect the answer "no": God will finish what he has begun.

decisions.choice: I would never ...; I would never close the womb
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions, which expect the answer "no", into statements.

records.source: שִׂמְח֧וּ אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם וְגִ֥ילוּ בָ֖הּ כָּל־אֹהֲבֶ֑יהָ שִׂ֤ישׂוּ אִתָּהּ֙ מָשׂ֔וֹשׂ כָּל־הַמִּֽתְאַבְּלִ֖ים עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad in her, all [ones] loving her; exult with her [in] joy, all the [ones] mourning over her,
pieces: Celebrate with Jerusalem and be glad over her, all who love her. \q Join in her great joy, all who have grieved for her,

L.10: Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad in her, all [you who] love her; \q exult with her [in] joy, all [you who] mourn over her,

R.10: Be happy with Jerusalem! Celebrate because of her, all of you who love her! \q You have been sad about her, but now you can share her great joy.

decisions.choice: rejoice, be glad, exult: a call to joy that runs on into verse 11
decisions.reason: Three verbs of joy are piled up. The call continues into verse 11, which gives its purpose: that they may share in Jerusalem's comfort.

decisions.choice: those who mourn over her: the faithful who grieved for ruined Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Mourning for Zion's ruin marks the faithful (57:18; 61:2-3; Lamentations 1:4). Now their grief turns to joy.

decisions.choice: You have been sad about her, but now
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the change from mourning to joy that the verse implies, and ends the sentence here.

records.source: לְמַ֤עַן תִּֽינְקוּ֙ וּשְׂבַעְתֶּ֔ם מִשֹּׁ֖ד תַּנְחֻמֶ֑יהָ לְמַ֧עַן תָּמֹ֛צּוּ וְהִתְעַנַּגְתֶּ֖ם מִזִּ֥יז כְּבוֹדָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: so that you may nurse and be satisfied from [the] breast of her consolations, so that you may drain and delight yourselves from [the] abundance of her glory.
pieces: so that you may feed at her breast and find comfort and be full, \q and draw your fill and revel in her rich glory.

L.11: so that you may nurse and be satisfied from the breast of her consolations, \q so that you may drink deeply and take delight from the abundance of her glory.

R.11: Jerusalem will be like a mother to you. She will comfort you as a mother feeds her baby. \q You will be full and satisfied with all the good things she has.

decisions.choice: the abundance of her glory: Jerusalem's rich supply, pictured as a nursing mother's flowing milk
decisions.reason: The word translated "abundance" occurs only here; it may mean the nipple, or the flow of milk. "Glory" here includes wealth and plenty, as in verse 12 ("the glory of the nations") and 61:6.

decisions.choice: the breast of her consolations: comfort given as a mother feeds a child
decisions.reason: Jerusalem is pictured as a mother who nurses her children (60:16; 49:23). Verse 13 shows that the comfort is God's own.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem will be like a mother to you
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture of Jerusalem as a nursing mother explicit and begins a new sentence.

records.source: כִּֽי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִ֣י נֹטֶֽה־אֵ֠לֶיהָ כְּנָהָ֨ר שָׁל֜וֹם וּכְנַ֧חַל שׁוֹטֵ֛ף כְּב֥וֹד גּוֹיִ֖ם וִֽינַקְתֶּ֑ם עַל־צַד֙ תִּנָּשֵׂ֔אוּ וְעַל־בִּרְכַּ֖יִם תְּשָׁעֳשָֽׁעוּ׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh: Look, I [am] extending to her like a river peace, and like an overflowing torrent [the] glory of nations; and you will nurse; on [the] hip you will be carried, and on [the] knees you will be dandled.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Look, I will make peace flow to her like a river, \q and the wealth of the nations like a stream in flood. You will feed at her breast; \q she will carry you at her side \q and play with you on her knees.

L.12: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] about to extend peace to her like a river, \q and the glory of [the] nations like an overflowing torrent; and you will nurse; \q on [the] hip you will be carried, \q and on [the] knees you will be dandled.

R.12: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I will give Jerusalem peace that flows like a river. The riches of the nations will pour into her like a flooding stream. \q You will be like babies that nurse at their mother's breast. \q She will carry you on her hip and play with you on her lap.

decisions.choice: peace like a river; the glory of the nations: lasting well-being and the wealth of the nations flowing into Zion
decisions.reason: Compare 48:18, where peace like a river was what Israel lost by not listening. "The glory of the nations" is their wealth, brought to Zion (60:5, 11; 61:6).

decisions.choice: carried on the hip, dandled on the knees: the care a mother gives an infant
decisions.reason: Small children were carried on the hip or side (60:4) and played with on the lap. The people are Zion's children (verse 8).

decisions.choice: Jerusalem; You will be like babies
decisions.reason: Readable names the city meant by "her" and makes the picture of nursing a comparison.

records.heading: Comfort for Zion and the gathering of the nations

records.source: כְּאִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִמּ֖וֹ תְּנַחֲמֶ֑נּוּ כֵּ֤ן אָֽנֹכִי֙ אֲנַ֣חֶמְכֶ֔ם וּבִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֖ם תְּנֻחָֽמוּ׃
records.gloss: Like a man whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you, and in Jerusalem you will be comforted.
pieces: Just as a mother comforts her own, \q so I myself will comfort you; \q in Jerusalem you will be comforted.

L.13: Like one whom his mother comforts, \q so I will comfort you, \q and in Jerusalem you will be comforted.

R.13: I will comfort you just as a mother comforts her son or daughter. \q You will find comfort in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: as a mother comforts, so I will comfort you: God's own comfort is pictured as a mother's
decisions.reason: In verses 11-12 Jerusalem is the mother; now God himself comforts like a mother (49:15; 42:14). The word "comfort" comes three times in the verse and echoes the opening of this part of the book (40:1; 51:3, 12).

decisions.choice: one whom his mother comforts: a child of any age, even a grown person
decisions.reason: The word usually means a man or person, not an infant. The picture moves from a nursing baby (verses 11-12) to anyone who is comforted by his mother.

decisions.choice: I myself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the full, emphatic form of "I"; Balanced shows the emphasis with "I myself".

records.source: וּרְאִיתֶם֙ וְשָׂ֣שׂ לִבְּכֶ֔ם וְעַצְמוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם כַּדֶּ֣שֶׁא תִפְרַ֑חְנָה וְנוֹדְעָ֤ה יַד־יְהוָה֙ אֶת־עֲבָדָ֔יו וְזָעַ֖ם אֶת־אֹיְבָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And you will see, and your heart will rejoice, and your bones like the grass will sprout; and the hand of Yahweh will be known with his servants, and he will be indignant with his enemies.
pieces: You will see this and your hearts will be glad; \q your bones will spring up like new grass. \q It will be known that the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants, \q but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be furious with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies.

L.14: And you will see, and your heart will rejoice, \q and your bones will sprout like [new] grass; \q and the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be made known with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rage against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies.

R.14: When you see this, you will be very happy. \q Your bodies will grow strong again, like grass that grows in spring. \q Everyone will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s power is with those who serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies.

decisions.choice: your bones will sprout like grass: your whole being will be renewed
decisions.reason: The bones stand for the body and the whole person (58:11; Proverbs 3:8; 15:30). Dried-up bones flourish again like fresh grass after rain.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD with his servants: his power shown on behalf of those who serve him
decisions.reason: "Hand" means power. "His servants" here are the faithful of verses 2 and 5, set against "his enemies" (65:8-15).

decisions.choice: Your bodies will grow strong again; the LORD's power
decisions.reason: Readable explains the bones as the body and the hand as power.

records.source: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בָּאֵ֣שׁ יָב֔וֹא וְכַסּוּפָ֖ה מַרְכְּבֹתָ֑יו לְהָשִׁ֤יב בְּחֵמָה֙ אַפּ֔וֹ וְגַעֲרָת֖וֹ בְּלַהֲבֵי־אֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: For look, Yahweh in fire will come, and like the storm-wind his chariots, to return in fury his anger and his rebuke in flames of fire.
pieces: Look! {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} comes in fire, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chariots sweep in like a storm, \q to give vent to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger in fury \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rebuke in tongues of fire.

L.15: For look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come in fire, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chariots like the storm wind, \q to pay back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger in fury, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rebuke in flames of fire.

R.15: Look! {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is coming with fire! \q His chariots are coming like a storm. \q He will pay back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning anger. \q He will punish them with flames of fire.

decisions.choice: the LORD comes in fire with chariots like the storm: God comes as a warrior to judge
decisions.reason: Fire and storm mark God's coming in 29:6; 30:27-30; Psalm 18:9-16; 50:3; and Habakkuk 3:8, where his chariots are victory. Paul uses this picture of the Lord's return in 2 Thessalonians 1:7-8.

decisions.choice: to pay back: to return his anger on the guilty, to give it full force
decisions.reason: The verb means "to cause to return". It can mean to pay back (as in verse 6) or to let anger loose; either way his enemies receive what they earned.

decisions.choice: pay back his enemies; punish them
decisions.reason: Readable names those who receive his anger ("his enemies", from verse 14) and says what his rebuke does.

records.source: כִּ֤י בָאֵשׁ֙ יְהוָ֣ה נִשְׁפָּ֔ט וּבְחַרְבּ֖וֹ אֶת־כָּל־בָּשָׂ֑ר וְרַבּ֖וּ חַֽלְלֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: For by fire Yahweh will enter into judgment, and by his sword, with all flesh; and many will be [the] slain of Yahweh.
pieces: By fire and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sword {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bring all humanity to judgment, \q and those struck down by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be many.

L.16: For by fire {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will enter into judgment, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sword, with all flesh; \q and many will be the slain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.16: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will judge all people with fire and with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sword. \q Many people will be killed by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: enter into judgment with all flesh: judge the whole human race
decisions.reason: "All flesh" means all humankind (40:5-6; 49:26). The same phrase comes again in verses 23 and 24, where all flesh worships God and sees the fate of the rebels.

decisions.choice: his sword, the slain of the LORD: God pictured as a warrior
decisions.reason: God's sword is a picture of his judgment (27:1; 34:5-6; Jeremiah 25:31-33).

records.source: הַמִּתְקַדְּשִׁ֨ים וְהַמִּֽטַּהֲרִ֜ים אֶל־הַגַּנּ֗וֹת אַחַ֤ר אַחַת֙ בַּתָּ֔וֶךְ אֹֽכְלֵי֙ בְּשַׂ֣ר הַחֲזִ֔יר וְהַשֶּׁ֖קֶץ וְהָעַכְבָּ֑ר יַחְדָּ֥ו יָסֻ֖פוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: The [ones] consecrating themselves and the [ones] purifying themselves to the gardens, after one in the middle, eating the flesh of the pig and the detestable thing and the mouse, together will come to an end, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Those who set themselves apart and cleanse themselves to enter the gardens, following the one in the center, \q who eat pork, vile creatures and mice, \q will perish together, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.17: Those who consecrate themselves and purify themselves [to go] to the gardens, after one in the middle, \q eating the flesh of the pig and the detestable thing and the mouse, \q together they will come to an end, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.17: Some people make themselves holy and clean so they can worship false gods in their gardens. They follow a leader who stands in the middle of the group. \q They eat pork, mice and other disgusting things. \q All of them will die together, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: consecrate and purify themselves for the gardens: prepare for pagan rites in sacred gardens
decisions.reason: Isaiah condemns worship in gardens in 1:29 and 65:3. The people perform rites of purification, but for the worship of other gods.

decisions.choice: after one in the middle: following a leader of the rites who stands in the center
alternatives: following a priestess in the center
behind an image in the middle
decisions.reason: The phrase is obscure. The written Hebrew text has the masculine form of "one" and the reading tradition the feminine, which could point to a priest or a priestess, or to a goddess or image set in the middle of the garden. The sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: the pig, the detestable thing and the mouse: unclean foods eaten in pagan rites
decisions.reason: The pig and the mouse were unclean (Leviticus 11:7, 29), and "detestable thing" is the word used for unclean creatures in Leviticus 11:10-13. Compare 65:4.

decisions.choice: so they can worship false gods in their gardens; a leader who stands in the middle of the group
decisions.reason: Readable says what the garden rites were and takes "one in the middle" as a leader, as Balanced does.

records.source: וְאָנֹכִ֗י מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם֙ וּמַחְשְׁבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם בָּאָ֕ה לְקַבֵּ֥ץ אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם וְהַלְּשֹׁנ֑וֹת וּבָ֖אוּ וְרָא֥וּ אֶת־כְּבוֹדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I, their deeds and their thoughts, [it] is coming to gather all the nations and the tongues; and they will come and they will see my glory.
pieces: I, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} part, know their deeds and their schemes. The time is coming for gathering every nation and language, and they will come and look on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory.

L.18: And I, their deeds and their thoughts ... [the time] is coming to gather all the nations and the tongues, and they will come and see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory.

R.18: I know everything they do and think. The time is coming when I will gather people from every nation and every language. They will come and see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory.

decisions.choice: And I, their deeds and their thoughts: I know their deeds and thoughts
alternatives: I will punish their deeds and thoughts
because of their deeds and thoughts, I am coming
decisions.reason: The sentence has no verb. A word like "know" seems to be understood (37:28; Psalm 139:2); some ancient versions supply it. The broken sentence may show strong feeling. The sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: it is coming: the time has come for the gathering
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine with no stated subject; "the time" is a natural subject. Some read "I am coming", as in the Septuagint.

decisions.choice: all nations and tongues will come and see my glory: the nations gathered to the LORD
decisions.reason: Compare 2:2-3; 40:5; 60:3. Peoples "of every language" recall the scattering at Babel (Genesis 11:1-9), now reversed in worship (Zechariah 8:23; Revelation 7:9).

decisions.choice: know
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "know", the verb that the broken sentence seems to imply (meaning decision m1). Literal leaves the gap.

decisions.choice: I will gather
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who gathers, as the context makes plain.

records.source: וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י בָהֶ֜ם א֗וֹת וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֣י מֵהֶ֣ם׀פְּ֠לֵיטִים אֶֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֞ם תַּרְשִׁ֨ישׁ פּ֥וּל וְל֛וּד מֹ֥שְׁכֵי קֶ֖שֶׁת תֻּבַ֣ל וְיָוָ֑ן הָאִיִּ֣ים הָרְחֹקִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־שָׁמְע֤וּ אֶת־שִׁמְעִי֙ וְלֹא־רָא֣וּ אֶת־כְּבוֹדִ֔י וְהִגִּ֥ידוּ אֶת־כְּבוֹדִ֖י בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will set among them a sign, and I will send from them survivors to the nations, Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, drawers of [the] bow, Tubal and Javan, the coastlands, the distant [ones], who have not heard my report and have not seen my glory; and they will declare my glory among the nations.
pieces: I will put a sign among them. From them I will send survivors out to the nations: to Tarshish, to Pul and to Lud, the people who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, and to the far coastlands that have not heard the news of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or seen {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory. They will tell of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory among the nations.

L.19: And I will set a sign among them, and I will send survivors from them to the nations: Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw [the] bow, Tubal and Javan, the distant coastlands that have not heard {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fame and have not seen {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory; and they will declare {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory among the nations.

R.19: I will put a sign among them. I will send some of the survivors to the nations. I will send them to Tarshish, Pul and Lud, where people are skilled with bows. I will send them to Tubal and Greece, and to lands far away. The people there have never heard about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or seen {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory. The survivors will tell the nations about {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory.

decisions.choice: a sign: a mark of God's act that the nations will see, not further described
decisions.reason: The sign is not explained. It may be the judgment and deliverance of verses 15-18, or the survivors themselves, sent out as witnesses (8:18; 11:10-12). The sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Tubal, Javan: peoples at the far edges of the known world
decisions.reason: Tarshish lay far to the west by sea (23:1-14; Jonah 1:3). Lud and Put (a people of Africa) appear together as soldiers in Jeremiah 46:9 and Ezekiel 27:10; 30:5. Tubal was in Asia Minor (Ezekiel 27:13), and Javan is Greece and the Greek coastlands (Genesis 10:2-4). The places stand for the whole world, west and north.

decisions.choice: Pul: the Hebrew name is kept
decisions.reason: "Pul" is not known as a nation elsewhere. The Septuagint reads "Put", the African people named with Lud in Jeremiah 46:9, and it may read "Meshech", a people paired with Tubal (Ezekiel 27:13; 38:2), where the Hebrew has "who draw the bow". The Hebrew is followed here.

decisions.choice: Greece; lands far away
decisions.reason: Readable gives the modern name for Javan, and says "lands far away" for the coastlands, as elsewhere in Isaiah.

records.source: וְהֵבִ֣יאוּ אֶת־כָּל־אֲחֵיכֶ֣ם מִכָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֣ם׀מִנְחָ֣ה׀לַֽיהוָ֡ה בַּסּוּסִ֡ים וּ֠בָרֶכֶב וּבַצַּבִּ֨ים וּבַפְּרָדִ֜ים וּבַכִּרְכָּר֗וֹת עַ֣ל הַ֥ר קָדְשִׁ֛י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָבִיאוּ֩ בְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֛ה בִּכְלִ֥י טָה֖וֹר בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they will bring all your brothers from all the nations [as] an offering to Yahweh, on horses and in chariot[s] and in litters and on mules and on camels, to [the] mountain of my holiness, Jerusalem, says Yahweh, just as the sons of Israel bring the offering in a clean vessel [to the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: They will bring all your kin out of every nation as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will come on horses, in chariots and covered carts, on mules and on swift camels, to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain, Jerusalem, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} bring grain offerings to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in clean vessels.

L.20: And they will bring all {{gender:your brothers and sisters|your brothers}} from all the nations [as] an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, on horses and in chariots and in litters and on mules and on camels, to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain, Jerusalem, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel bring the offering in a clean vessel [to] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.20: They will bring all your fellow Israelites back from all the nations. They will bring them as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will ride on horses, in chariots and wagons, and on mules and camels. They will come to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain in Jerusalem, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It will be like when the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} bring grain offerings to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in clean dishes.

decisions.choice: your brothers: fellow Israelites scattered among the nations
decisions.reason: The survivors from the nations (verse 19) bring back the scattered people of Israel (11:12; 43:5-7; 49:22; 60:4, 9).

decisions.choice: as an offering in a clean vessel: the returning exiles are presented to God like a holy gift
decisions.reason: The nations bring Israel's scattered people to God as worshipers bring a grain offering in a ritually clean vessel. Paul speaks of his work among the Gentiles in the language of this verse (Romans 15:16).

decisions.choice: litters, camels: covered carts or carrying chairs; swift camels
decisions.reason: The first word is used of covered wagons in Numbers 7:3. The last word occurs only here; it seems to mean fast-running camels or dromedaries.

decisions.choice: your fellow Israelites; the temple of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says who "your brothers" are (meaning decision m1) and calls the house of the LORD the temple.

records.source: וְגַם־מֵהֶ֥ם אֶקַּ֛ח לַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים לַלְוִיִּ֖ם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And also from them I will take for priests, for Levites, says Yahweh.
pieces: And I will even take some of them to be priests and Levites, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: And also from them I will take [some] for priests [and] for Levites, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: I will even choose some of them to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests and Levites, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: some of them: perhaps from the nations who bring the exiles, perhaps from the exiles themselves
decisions.reason: "Them" may be the people of the nations (verses 18-19) or the scattered Israelites they bring home (verse 20). If it is the nations, God will even make foreigners his priests (56:6-7; 61:6). The word "also" suggests something surprising, but the sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: priests and Levites: those who served at the altar and in the temple
decisions.reason: Under the law only descendants of Aaron could be priests, and the other Levites served beside them (Numbers 3:5-10; 18:1-7).

decisions.choice: to serve me
decisions.reason: Readable says what priests and Levites do.

records.source: כִּ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם הַ֠חֳדָשִׁים וְהָאָ֨רֶץ הַחֲדָשָׁ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֛ה עֹמְדִ֥ים לְפָנַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה כֵּ֛ן יַעֲמֹ֥ד זַרְעֲכֶ֖ם וְשִׁמְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: For just as the heavens, the new [ones], and the earth, the new [one], which I [am] making, [are] standing before me, declares Yahweh, so will stand your offspring and your name.
pieces: The new heavens and the new earth that I am about to make will stand firm in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q in the same way your descendants and your name will stand firm.

L.22: For just as the new heavens and the new earth that I [am] making will endure before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q so your offspring and your name will endure.

R.22: I am going to make a new heaven and a new earth, and they will last in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q In the same way, your descendants and your name will last too.

decisions.choice: the new heavens and the new earth: the renewed creation promised in 65:17
decisions.reason: The promise of 65:17 returns here. Peter and John take it up (2 Peter 3:13; Revelation 21:1).

decisions.choice: endure: last and remain, as God's new creation will
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for both: as the new creation stands before God, so will Israel's descendants and name. Compare 48:19 and 56:5, where a lasting name is promised.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה מִֽדֵּי־חֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ בְּחָדְשׁ֔וֹ וּמִדֵּ֥י שַׁבָּ֖ת בְּשַׁבַּתּ֑וֹ יָב֧וֹא כָל־בָּשָׂ֛ר לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת לְפָנַ֖י אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it will be [that] from new moon in its new moon, and from sabbath in its sabbath, all flesh will come to bow down before me, says Yahweh.
pieces: Month after month at the new moon, \q and week after week on the Sabbath, \q all humanity will come to bow in worship before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.23: And it will be [that] from new moon to new moon \q and from Sabbath to Sabbath, \q all flesh will come to bow down before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.23: At every new moon festival and on every Sabbath day, \q all people will come to worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: new moon and Sabbath: the regular monthly and weekly days of worship
decisions.reason: The new moon began each month with offerings (Numbers 28:11-15), and the Sabbath was the weekly day of rest. The same feasts were condemned when kept without obedience (1:13-14); now they are kept by all peoples.

decisions.choice: all flesh will come to bow down: all peoples worship the LORD
decisions.reason: In verse 16 "all flesh" faces God's judgment; here all flesh comes to worship him (45:23; Psalm 65:3; Zechariah 14:16).

records.source: וְיָצְא֣וּ וְרָא֔וּ בְּפִגְרֵי֙ הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַפֹּשְׁעִ֖ים בִּ֑י כִּ֣י תוֹלַעְתָּ֞ם לֹ֣א תָמ֗וּת וְאִשָּׁם֙ לֹ֣א תִכְבֶּ֔ה וְהָי֥וּ דֵרָא֖וֹן לְכָל־בָּשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: And they will go out and they will look on [the] corpses of the men, the [ones] rebelling against me; for their worm will not die, and their fire will not be quenched, and they will be an abhorrence to all flesh.
pieces: Then they will go out and gaze on the corpses of the people who rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q For their worm will not die, nor will their fire be put out, \q and they will be a horror to every living being.

L.24: And they will go out and look on the corpses of the men who rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q for their worm will not die and their fire will not be quenched, \q and they will be an abhorrence to all flesh.

R.24: Then the worshipers will go out and see the dead bodies of those who turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q The worms in those bodies will never die. The fire that burns them will never go out. \q Everyone who sees them will be disgusted.

decisions.choice: their worm will not die and their fire will not be quenched: the endless end of the rebels
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes these words in Mark 9:48 of Gehenna, the valley outside Jerusalem whose name came to stand for final judgment. The word for "abhorrence" occurs elsewhere only in Daniel 12:2, of those who rise "to everlasting contempt".

decisions.choice: they will go out and look: those who come to worship (verse 23) see the fate of the rebels
decisions.reason: The worshipers leave Jerusalem and see the bodies of the rebels outside the city. When this chapter is read in the synagogue, verse 23 is read again after verse 24 so that the book ends on worship, not on judgment. The text itself is not changed.

decisions.choice: the worshipers
decisions.reason: Readable names those who go out: the people of all nations who come to worship in verse 23.

decisions.choice: The worms in those bodies will never die; Everyone who sees them will be disgusted
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the worm and the abhorrence are.
